name: Doty Ravine Preserve — monthly
description: Placer Land Trust preserve north of Lincoln, CA. Process-based restoration (beaver dam analogues + natural beaver recolonization) beginning ~2014 reconnected ~60 acres of floodplain along Doty Ravine, a tributary of Coon Creek.

analysisAreas.label: Restored floodplain + downstream corridor
analysisAreas.notes: The ~60-acre reconnected floodplain west of Gladding Rd plus the downstream corridor to the tight frame's west edge, which shows improvement over time (approximate footprint, inferred — replace with parcel/project boundary when available).

analysisAreas.label: Upstream corridor (control)
analysisAreas.notes: Riparian corridor east of Gladding Rd, upstream of the floodplain work — same stream, no floodplain reconnection. Distinguishes restoration effect from riparian-corridors-in-general. Verify no PBR occurred here.

analysisAreas.label: Whole landscape (reference)
analysisAreas.notes: Nearly the full tight-view extent minus the irrigated pasture block in the northeast (its artificial greenness would mask the climate signal). Tracks the overall drought/climate signal, the baseline the treatment should diverge from.

notes: Center set on the preserve reach of Doty Ravine: 'off Gladding and Manzanita Roads, near Manzanita Cemetery' (cemetery at 38.9440, -121.3039 per OSM), stream at lat ~38.939 there. Verified against calibration frames 2025-Q3. Monthly-cadence variant of doty-ravine; same AOI, views, events, and analysis areas.
